newsitem.title: USA: USX-U.S. Steel sees steel operations improving.
newsitem.headline: USX-U.S. Steel sees steel operations improving.

text.p: USX-U.S. Steel Group said Tuesday that it expects its steel operations to benefit in the fourth quarter from greater demand, lower costs and higher prices.

Company Chairman Thomas Usher said in a statement that the results also should be helped as the company recovers from major outages it experienced in the third quarter at its three largest blast furnaces.
Usher said the company should see better results from lower costs through reduced purchases of semifinished steel and by previously-announced price increases.

For the third quarter, the company posted net income of $70 million, or $0.76 per primary share, on revenues of $1.61 billion. In the same period the prior year, the company reported net income of $85 million, or $0.98 per primary share, on revenues of $1.62 billion.

"The blast furnace relines prevented the Steel Group from taking full advantage of continued strong market demand during the third quarter," Usher said. "Nevertheless, by supplementing our own production with purchases of semifinished steel, the Steel Group minimized the negative impact on its customers."
